source.title: Raising Bars, Not Parameters: LilMoo Compact Language Model for Hindi
source.authors: Shiza Fatimah; Aniket Sen; Sophia Falk; Florian Mai; Lucie Flek; Nicholas Kluge Corrêa

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The authors use DeepSeek scaling heuristics to derive shared batch-size and learning-rate settings, but do not test the loss-scaling or compute-optimal allocation claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative training-loss curves, not held-out loss power-law fits. It does not sweep model size or compute to fit or validate scaling laws. Its downstream benchmark evaluations and the scaling heuristics used to set hyperparameters do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper trains two ~670M-parameter Hindi models with a fixed recipe each. It uses DeepSeek compute-based power laws only to set batch size and learning rate, and never validates them. There is no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute, no loss-scaling fit, no extrapolation, and no allocation or shape comparison. Its loss curves are within-run training loss. Downstream scores are tracked over checkpoints, not as a function of scale or loss. The Qwen compute comparison sets models with different data and recipes side by side; it is not a scaling test.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that compact Hindi models trained from scratch with curated data outperform Qwen2.5/3 baselines with far less compute. They also find that adding high-quality English data helps most benchmarks but hurts the culturally grounded Global PIQA. They say generalization to other languages and scales remains uncertain.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce the original loss-scaling measurements; it uses DeepSeek compute heuristics to choose batch size and learning rate and reports training curves for two recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The two training recipes show different loss-curve behavior; the multi-stage recipe's data-mixture changes coincide with discontinuous loss shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: In a multi-stage pretraining recipe, training loss shows discontinuous jumps at data-mixture changes; the single-stage recipe improves steadily.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changes in data mixture during multi-stage pretraining produce discontinuities in training-loss trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: LilMoo models trained with about 1.3e21 FLOPs score higher on aggregate Hindi NPM than Qwen3-0.6B-Base (about 1.3e23 FLOPs). The compute ratio is about 100x, across differing data and recipes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-specific curated pretraining can beat much higher-compute multilingual models of similar size on target-language benchmarks.

record.problems: Only two recipes at approximately 670 million parameters are trained; there is no size, token-budget, or compute sweep or scaling-law fit. The reported loss curves are training loss and plotted values are not provided in text. The authors note resource constraints limited extensive ablations.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result was omitted.

untested.parts: No loss fit across parameters, tokens or compute; one model size only.
No small-run fits used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison of parameter/token splits.
A 'deep and slim' shape was chosen from prior literature; no shape ablation at fixed parameters.
Repeated data (5 epochs) is used, but no power-law fit in this regime or any other.
Benchmarks are tracked over training checkpoints, but not as a function of model scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices or setups.

record.verdict_notes: The DeepSeek power laws for batch size and learning rate versus compute are applied as tools; this is T4. The paper does mention a held-out validation set evaluated every 5,000 steps, but reports no validation-loss values. Figure 1 shows training loss.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute over several orders of magnitude; the reported curves are training loss.
No small-run fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or comparison of parameter/token allocations.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law tests in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream benchmarks are tracked during training, but the paper does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices or setups.

rows.subject: LilMoo-v0.1
rows.operation_detail: Single-stage Hindi-only pretraining; reports training-loss curve over training.
rows.note: The text describes steady improvement over time with no major loss spikes or rollbacks; plotted values are not given in text.
rows.check: Within-run training-loss curve for one model size; it cannot show a power law across parameters, tokens or compute. 'observed' has no version to apply to, so the state is cannot_determine.

rows.subject: LilMoo-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Multi-stage Hindi-English pretraining; reports training-loss curve over training.
rows.note: The text describes discontinuous loss jumps attributed to changes in data mixtures and differences in average cross-entropy; it also reports no major loss spikes or rollbacks.
rows.check: Within-run training-loss curve with jumps at data-mixture changes; it bears on no version. 'partial' has no referent, so the state is cannot_determine.
